nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Long summer days power plankton blooms in the fjords and plant growth on the shores.

nodes.name: Glacial meltwater
nodes.desc: Runoff from the Harding Icefield glaciers carries rock flour minerals into the fjords. The park page says this supports phytoplankton.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Bare ground left by retreating glaciers gains soil as lichens, mosses and nitrogen-fixing alders arrive, and later supports forest.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, animals and spawned-out salmon, returning nutrients to the soil and streams.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae that bloom in the fjords and nearshore waters, fed in part by minerals in glacial meltwater. They are the base of the marine food web.

nodes.name: Salmonberry
nodes.desc: A berry shrub of the coastal forest and shrub thickets. Its fruit is food for bears and birds.

nodes.name: Fireweed
nodes.desc: A tall wildflower that colonizes open, disturbed ground such as newly exposed land.

nodes.name: Sitka spruce
nodes.desc: The dominant conifer of the coastal forest, which develops on ground that glaciers have left behind.

nodes.name: Krill and zooplankton
nodes.desc: Small drifting crustaceans that graze phytoplankton. They feed humpback whales, young salmon, puffins and schooling fish.

nodes.name: Bay mussel
nodes.desc: Filter-feeding shellfish on rocky shores that eat plankton. Sea otters eat mussels.

nodes.name: Pacific sand lance
nodes.desc: A small schooling fish that eats zooplankton and is prey for many seabirds, fish and marine mammals.

nodes.name: Hoary marmot
nodes.desc: A large ground squirrel of alpine meadows that eats plants and is prey for bears and other carnivores.

nodes.name: Mountain goat
nodes.desc: A steep-terrain herbivore that grazes grasses, herbs and shrubs, and browses conifer twigs. Bears and eagles may take kids.

nodes.name: Pink salmon
nodes.desc: Feeds on plankton, invertebrates and small fish at sea, then returns to streams to spawn. Spawned-out carcasses feed bears and stream life.

nodes.name: Tufted puffin
nodes.desc: A diving seabird that nests in burrows on cliffs and islands. Adults eat squid and krill, and chicks are fed mostly fish such as sand lance.

nodes.name: Black-legged kittiwake
nodes.desc: A surface-feeding gull that eats fish such as capelin, herring and sand lance in the Gulf of Alaska.

nodes.name: Sea otter
nodes.desc: Eats mostly marine invertebrates such as urchins, crabs, clams and mussels. Orcas are its main predator.

nodes.name: Steller sea lion
nodes.desc: An opportunistic predator of schooling fish, including pollock, herring, sand lance and salmon. Orcas are the main predator.

nodes.name: Humpback whale
nodes.desc: A gulp-feeder that eats krill and small schooling fish such as herring and sand lance. Orcas hunt calves.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: Eats mostly fish, then waterfowl and other birds, and scavenges carrion. Often steals food from other animals.

nodes.name: Orca
nodes.desc: The top marine predator of the park waters. GloBI records show it eating whales, seals, sea lions, porpoises and sea otters.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats salmon, berries, marmots and mountain goats. It carries salmon carcasses into the forest.
